svg.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: trim test
svg.desc: Testing the notebook's claim that trimming loses the user's name. The notebook says so but never asks for the name after trimming. Test A, the notebook's own five-turn chat: the trim keeps the last two messages, and the last answer already says 'Your name is Alice', yet asked again, Claude said it didn't know the name and that its earlier answer had been wrong. Test B, the first four turns only: on Claude the trim kept two messages, neither mentioning Alice, and the model said it didn't know; on Groq a long answer alone was over the 300-token budget and the trim kept no messages at all.
svg.text: Does trimming really lose the name? The notebook never asked
the notebook's note: trimming removes old messages, so the user's name is LOST
kept 2: 'remind me what my name is?'
asked again: 'I don't know your name…
In A the name survives the trim inside the model's own previous answer, and the model still refused it, because
nothing the user said supports it. In B a single long answer can exceed the 300-token budget, and
start_on='human' then leaves an empty history.
